Hike is very rewarding but equally hard if you do the entire trail.
Smokey Hollow - Walmart to waterfall and back. 1hr6min there. Slower back. 2hr22 total. Lots of variety. Little bridges, stairs. I like the rocky section behind Walmart ponds.
Beautiful trail! Gets very busy near the falls.

Great morning run. Trails are pretty easy and well maintained but plenty of elevation gains and drops throughout. A few stretches (especially at the start/end) where you could roll an ankle so be careful. But a beautiful hike
Hard to park at peak times

Very very muddy but doable!  Easy parking at either end for P2P.   Sunny and 26C.
So peaceful, not many people on the trail. Great views and lots of wildlife presence

Great hike, starts off at the waterfall and follows the river. Trail has lots of ups and downs so be ready for it! 
Eventually the river ends and it goes through more of a forest. Recommend this trail!
Lots of mud (understandably).  Creek is running beautifully fast.
Muddy as it rained hard night before
One of our fav hikes in the area
So awesome. Must visit the trail at Spring time. Lot of water gushing through the creek. So peaceful and relaxing. Highly recommended.
Nice trail, long and intermediate. Terrain is rocky with tree vines coming out of the ground in many places. Careful footwork is important to avoid injury.
Great. Challenging tough
Definitely a moderate trail with lots of elevation/inclines, roots and rocks! The parking lot is small - maybe 15 cars max but great if you ca get a spot. It was a great hike and experience!
Great trail, big climbs, small parking lot
I found this trail challenging in all the right ways. My kids and I went ages 10 and 8.  We completed the long route and it took us about 3 1/2 hrs
If it hadn’t rained past 3 days it would have been perfect
More challenging than I expected. I loved it and with all the side trails I’ll be back to explore them.
Very muddy in April!
Nice day out! Trail is very muddy, but great views of the waterfall at the end! Easy parking and not many people on the trail.
Snow covered and variable conditions under foot. Some mud, loose leaves but quite manageable.

This is a bit of a challenging hike because it has a lot of ups and downs and in March it’s very muddy and also very icy so it’s very slippery. There’s rocks and roots, but the high itself is very beautiful. It takes too along the grindstone creek definitely worth it but it’s not for the first time hiker.

Great trail. 
White tailed deers on site.
A little harder than intermittent level. Good balance of elevation and slight grade trails. Bring lots of water as it’s a long one!
Honestly just park at the waterdown Walmart because the trail can be very busy making it hard to park at the small trailhead lot

If you are looking for a hike with lots and lots of uphill sections this is the one for you! The first couple of kilometres are a bit crowded but once you get deeper into the trails it dies down. Such a beautiful spot at the beginning with the waterfall and creek! Parking lot is very small and filled up. Parked in the street nearby and had to walk about 4 minutes to the trail.
The parking lot is small. Took a while to get in with a full sized pickup, but we got in eventually. The trail is very hilly and all kinds of terrain. Beautiful scenery.

Moderately busy on a holiday Monday with crowds mostly gathering at the trailhead. Beautiful creek adjacent trail - a little twisty and knotty for those caring for ankles and knees, but many side trails to grab and explore. Many small hills to scale, enjoy the climb! For the dog walkers who don't scoop up after your pet, do better.

Great hike! Not easy to park and the first bit is very busy, but once you get past the people it’s great! Lots of up and down, tougher terrain, and different scenery. Can go shorter or longer depending on your preference and get a few different route options. Wasn’t buggy at all until dusk but then got pretty buggy.
Falls view and water sound were amazing
Parkings very hard, if you go up towards town behind the barber shop there’s municipal parking
Parking gets filled up fast. Come early or park downtown and walk to the trail head
Probably in the middle of easy and moderate hike. Make sure to be there early or else parking will be difficult. Maybe Max of 16 cars if drivers park properly lol. No washrooms
Quite narrow and rocky to start. Well marked. Good ups and downs. More elevation towards the waterfall.
Flowing river to swim the dogs. Some rocky terrain. Overall great moderate level difficulty hike
little boring

it was great to hike on this trail. elevarion is high. loved it.

Great. Lots of fun. Rugged. 90% is moderate, but there are a few big steep hills. Can get quite muddy and buggy. Make sure it hasn't rained for few days. LOTS of forks in trail, so make sure you have map.

Fast "late for school" march, took me 2hr15.
Very hilly. I might be dead now. But fun! And the very beginning is beautiful.
Awesome trail! If you’re looking for a fun but challenging trail run, this one’s for you. Great conditions, easy to navigate and basically empty.
Nice trail with some incline ‘opportunities’. Is very busy on the weekend.
Good hike, lots of roots & rocks on trail. Step carefully. Smokey Hollow Falls is really pretty!
Muddy . But great trail
Stormy girl approved :) awesome hike
Lots of up and down, lots of options, some water, some bridges, lots of roots. As long or short as you want, lots of trails to explore.

First real hike I’ve done near Toronto since moving here from Vancouver—if you know what real nature and elevation is, it is quite difficult to find anything around here that’s not a boring flat semi-industrialized walk. The parking at this trail junction seems pretty ugly and a bit sketchy, but almost no one was using it. Once you get away from the highway, it was actually decently nice, and saw virtually no one else except near the waterfall (which was our turnaround point for today)..because there’s a big parking area there. There’s some decent up and down, but quite mild vs an actual mountain—this is merely up and down the side of a ravine. But it’s good for what it is. Conditions were great, nice temp, no bugs. The blazes were mostly easy to follow and clearly posted, although there’s a few spots where it helped to have AllTrails/gps because the trails snake in multiple directions. Speaking of which—if I did this leg again I would just start from Snake road.

With a bit of everything, this is a challenging hike.  Lots of rocks, several hills and some easy trails to provide a bit of relief from the rocks. Keep an eye on the white blazes through Clappison Woods as there are a lot of other trails in there.  The final ascent along Grindstone Creek is beautiful with huge boulders and a noisy creek, ending at Great Falls.
Well marked and easy to follow! Lots of nice views and a great walk alongside the river, some deer in the area as well!

Lots of ups and downs! 
Big leg work out
Lots of side trails. Haed and steep start. Narrow parts with sharp drops, keep kids close.
Hard to park, but great trail

Very busy at the beginning of the trail by the river. But then all the kids got bored and left. Then very quiet trail except for that older gentleman who was concerned about the garbage. Very fun.

Without gps you’re going to take the wrong trail at least once. So either follow GPS or plan out the blazes.
Park in behind Walmart to access trail and avoid small parking lot. Very hilly. A few muddy spots but nothing impassable.

Parking filled up fast for an early Sunday morning. Had t wait about 10 minutes, but it was worth it.

Many muddy spots in the train, expected since it spring and there is a lot of run-off. 

The further you go on the trail the number of walker/hikers thins out.

Makes for great view and pictures.
Great trail with limited parking spots! Gear up! Make sure you are wearing hiking boots.

As always, water down to Smoky hollow is a tremendous trail. Beautiful views. Beautiful waterfall! Great challenging hike as of now. It's really muddy and super slippery so just be careful of that going up. The hills going up was like a treadmill on Max incline going down. The trail was like skiing on a steep mountain

Very muddy - wait at least a week. Rocky section next to walmart is great - my favourite. East of train tracks, mostly dry or hard snow up long hills. Middle section west of train tracks - fell - Lots and lots of mud. And slick icy steps up from road.
Nice hike with lots of hills and minimal city noise

went when it was very icy did not go far

Muddy right now but still a great trail.
Some ankle breakers of rocks near the loop but still a great walk.

I did the full 11 km. Not sure why it says I only got three maybe because I lost gps signal most of the way but honestly fantastic trail. Highly recommend a lot of UPS. A lot of downs. Very beautiful but overall very muddy fantastic views

Hiking boots ……muddy at times
But a great trail!
Loved it
Beautiful hike in great weather. A bit muddy in two short sections but more than possible with proper footwear.
Great hike, beautiful!

I parked behind the Walmart and started the trail there. There's numerous different trails to take when you first get into the bush. Some of the terrain is Rocky, and watch for tree roots. There's some ups and downs depending on which trail you take. I really enjoyed it with all the different colors. Further up, closer to the waterfall, there's a lot of rock in the creek. Makes for really nice scenery. My 6-year-old German Shepherd did it no problem.

The trail is very beautiful and I wouldve given it a higher rating if it weren't for two things. The first one is the size of the parking area at the waterdown trail start. It is very limited so I highly suggest arriving early so you don't have any parking issues because it is very difficult to find a different parking area once the lot is full. Second is the fact that the main creek and waterfall are at the very start of the trail. If you're mostly just after taking pictures of the falls and/or the river, then know that just extends to about an hour mark of the entire trail. After that, it's just mostly a bit of rugged terrain inside the forest. It's still beautiful though. But if you're the type that enjoy having a destination attraction like a fall or a river during your hike before coming back, then I suggest starting the trail at the back of Walmart parking lot heading towards the waterdown trail. Besides that, amazing trail. The small, crowded parking lot took some of the fun out of the hike but that's also preventable by just coming early.
Blue side trail doesn’t lead anywhere but the elevation climb is good
Very scenic trail. Not too busy on a Friday. Lots of roots and rocks and hills. Wish I had my poles.

Great out and back trail. We brought our dog who had no problem. The last km in the loop section is fairly rocky though. We arrived at 11am on a Thursday and the parking lot was empty. It was busier when we left and it took us just over 3 hours with lots of water breaks.

Really nice trails with different paths you can take to mix it up. Most of the trails are mot difficult but it is hilly and quite muddy (and even more muddy after some unexpected rainfall) so prepare for a slower hike. The waterfall is pretty and it’s nice to follow the path along the water for a while.
Such a beautiful hike; lots of elevation and scenic look outs!
The trail was really nice but the ponds at the halfway point weren’t super pretty and they were surrounded by big industrial buildings. The trail was longer than expected - closer to 8 miles.
Certain portions were more rugged than expected but we got a good workout.
Steep and challenging at times but great hike. Could imagine it to be quite tough after rainfall.

A great hike. The parking fills up quickly so it’s best to go early.
please park next to the residential street or main street as the parking lot for the trail is very busy

Come early for parking. Beautiful spot that was quiet in the morning. 
Does have rocky and muddy trails in areas so watch those ankles!

It is a beautiful trail. It can be completed in under 3 hours (for me it took longer as I had to stop for water breaks for my dog). I would recommend starting early in the am as it was hot and humid. The mosquitoes were wild so be prepared. If you make it to the end of the trail, you can do a quick stop in Walmart (I did to restock in water and apples). Parking is a little hectic so be patient.
A great trail. Bit buggy so consider bug repellant. Didn’t need hiking shoes.
It’s beautiful waterfall views and sounds for the first 40 minutes. I had a very humid day so I took a shortcut to come back. I have done the full trail and really enjoy it. Be prepared for hills.

A challenging terrain with lots of up and down. We completed the full trail in 3 hours 34 minutes. Overall we found the track difficult may be coz it was really hot today otherwise I feel on a nice cool day it will be a pleasant walk. Please be careful around fallen tress as you could entangle your legs and get sprain like I got on my ankles.

Beautiful, slightly muggy day. 7:40 am start with no cars in the parking lot and back around 10:40 with an almost full lot.  The lake loop portion of the hike was extremely buggy in comparison to the rest of the hike.
Mature maples, oak and hickory. Plenty of shade.
Beautiful up and downhills. Great falls view.
Super fun trail! Elevation the entire way with some nice water at the beginning. Crowded towards the end of our hike (around late morning).

Parking and the falls area starts to get busy after noon, but the further you walk into the hike the less people.

Really pretty river and falls, bout it though. The trail further was fun, but pond was pretty boring. Park uphill past the parking lot thats always full.

Great trail with multiple highlights. Fairly challenging in places - bring good shoes! The waterfall and the path along the creek are very nice and the area with the ponds at halfway has a bunch of different animals and birds.

This trail had great views, and was definitely up there in terms of difficulty. It was raining, so conditions were slick and muddy. A lot of hills and slopes, and very little flat terrain. The map was spot on.
Incredibly challenging trail. Beautiful views. Multiple steep climbs. Well worth the drive and hike.

We parked by Sealy Park. Waterdown Trail to Smokey Hollow was terrific! A little muddy in spots, but overall the trail path was fine. There are some challenging inclines, and big roots to traverse. Beautiful scenery and just a great hike!

Very muddy this time of year so wear supportive waterproof hiking boots. Gorgeous trail as always.

Early March 2024 there are parts that are extremely muddy, otherwise it is a fantastic trail.

I also noticed quite a bit of trash and dog poop bags left behind instead of put in the garbage where they belong.  LEAVE NOTHING BEHIND BUT YOUR FOOTPRINTS PEOPLE. Was nice but muddy

Waterproof gear recommended!

We did the first half of this trail on January 3, 2024 when the weather had consistently been around or just above freezing. Perhaps due to the freeze-thaw, the trail was very muddy.

The trail is extremely beautiful as it explores uphill, downhill, and creekside locations.

Overall, loved it. Good exercise going up and down the hills. Went on a rainy day, so some sections were really muddy and slippery. A plus was that we hardly saw any other people. Lots of rocks in some sections, would recommend hiking boots if you have them.

Wow, I’ve already finished almost all famous and popular “MODERATE” 12-km -ish in Southern Ontario and it was BY FARRR the best one. ! The fall colors are out of this world - so stunning! Be warned though, there are some steep hills that might be a bit much for beginners.

I followed the advice of others and parked at the Waterdown Walmart. Started the hike from the other side of the trail and it was perfect. Can’t wait to do it again, highly recommend!
Beautiful! A great variety of terrain, especially near the water. May be mucky.

Horrible parking by the falls, better to park near the Walmart super centre from the other side of the trail. That being said, it is a beautiful hike. Well marked trail, difficult terrain, waterfall and water flowing for the majority of the trail. Wonderful sound to dull out the new tone of traffic. By the falls there are few dodgy stairs and stair cases leading you down the trail, be careful with your pups. Misquitoes were a little rough later into nightfall but not unmanageable with a little spray. Trail markings around Walmart are a little dicey so the app is helpful around those corners. Phone died on the way out but it took a solid 4hours with 2 dogs and few breaks for photos. This hike is definitely not to be done in the winter months. At least not from the falls but maybe the other side of clappison woods, if you park at Walmart as previously mentioned. This hike is definitely going to be one of the faves moving forward. Happy trails everyone

Parked at Walmart and saw very few people until we neared the falls . Very busy at the falls end. 

Well marked with a number of hills.

Lots of elevation changes and some makeshift stairs along the way - legs will be sore tomorrow!
Outstanding hike I'm was so exhausted .Bring Boots bring boots very muddy.

First the good - you get a nice waterfall and a great workout on the Bruce Trail for most of the hike.

Downside? Well, there are a couple of sections near the tracks that could use some bushwhacking, so wear your long pants. There are a few muddy parts but none hard to walk around. It's not a loop so unless you walk through town you'll have to traverse the same terrain in reverse. And honestly, park in the plaza lot because the one at the waterfall suuuuuuccckkksssss and is way too small.

Lots of bugs,saw a deer, and we'll maintained trail!

Good mix of less incline, stairs & hilly areas. Lots of roots & bumpy terrain, easy to trip on without the right footwear or cognizance. Beautiful views though, lots of free flowing water. One of my favourites for sure.

Mostly dry. A few muddy but avoidable spots.

Loved the trail. We went after a rainy day and still the trail was in good condition.

Trail was beautiful and not too busy on a Friday afternoon. There were some spots that were a little muddy but it wasn’t too bad! Great workout as well with all the ups and downs.
Good work out, lots of up and downhill
Very good trail ‘’not muddy’’ these days are best to come

Nice waterfall though!
Still a little muddy in the low spots but beautiful nonetheless
Challenging hike, mostly muddy today, adding a slippery factor to it. Started at Mill St. & went for an hour then turned back. Many brought dogs, nice to see.  Absolutely picturesque river and falls.

This is an awesome Trail but not for the faint of heart. Lots of inclines in both directions. My glutes are screaming! Four stars because it’s extremely muddy in early spring - like suck-your-boots-off muddy.
Muddy but agree with the poster below— worth it! Definitely need hiking shoes

Some buddy parts on the way back later in the day. No long icy patches expect for a handful. Too many dogs off leash though.
Awesome trail by the river and in the forest. Some serious inclines so a great workout! Several very muddy spots but the mud was all frozen today :-)

I've done this one many times, it was a little muddy but only really a problem in a couple of the steep downhills.

Safe trail to go on a solo weekday hike :)

Very nice trail, lots of ups and downs. Roots and rocks WATCH YOUR STEP parking is nightmare!! They will ticket you if you park on side of the road

Beautiful location for a moderate hiking during the fall. The fall colors are absolutely gorgeous! The waterfall is not big enough, but beautiful.  Autumn leaves throughout the trail adds the beauty of this trail.

Amazing trail but very icy.  Crampons a must.  Beautiful waterfall at Mill Street entrance in Waterdown.  Took the river trail to a wooden bridge that crossed the creek.  Lots of stairs for the first 20 minutes of the walk but well worth the views and feeling of walking on the side of a cliff.
Beautiful trail, but covered in ice. Don’t go without ice spikes
You must bring your icers!!!
All mud and ice
very challenging especially in the muddy sections after you cross the river. Be prepared to do what feels like constant trekking up hills but a great experience

Forgot to stop recording at the end. We actually managed to do the whole trail, 11,5 km in total. Good workout with many elevation changes. Lots of snow on the trail, with some ice. Ice cleats and poles absolutely necessary.
If you are planning to do the entire 13 Kms back and forth, better be prepared coz it’s not an easy one. BUT what a beautiful hike! Love it. Ice cleats recommended in this weather!
Hills!
Gorgeous snow covered trail today. Not manageable for many without ice spikes.

Spectacular! The waterfall is gorgeous, and climbing behind it is fully possible! The trail is slippy but challenging. Once again, as I did in fall, I made it a "loop" by walking through town. However, Hamilton apparently doesn't really plow sidewalks which is ludicrous.
Awesome trail. It’s a winter wonderland out there. Wear ice cleats because some parts are steep and icy. We walked behind the frozen waterfall. Really cool

a thorough hike, lots of hills and curves, was so snowy today which made the views all the more stunning. A little slippery so I had to watch my footing. I got slightly side tracked at the end of the path but was able to stay on course overall.

Beautiful trail, lots of hills and declines made it memorable and great exercise! Micro-spikes are certainly necessary if attempting this trail in the winter. Possibility for link ups and longer stretches for sure.

Great hike! Recording is about 3km short as I stopped it rather than paused it by accident. Great 12km hike, very easy to follow the Bruce trail markings to stay on course and very sheltered from the cold wind the entire hike! BRING SPIKES, very icy and slippery hike.
Sooo beautiful! A bit slippery so make sure to wear proper footwear.

A fantastic trail. Can get very icy in winter, and would definitely recommend some sort of a traction device. The parking lot by Smokey Hollow is tiny (about 15 cars max), and it can be tricky to find alternate places to park.

Ran the trail multiple times, start of the trail is a descent with stairs. Use caution when going down the stairs if there has been a melt and then a freeze with any kind of snowfall. Gets very icy. And the snow will hide that ice. Slightly technical, watch your footing and lift your feet up, easy to trip here. The first mile has lots of Medium sized rocks poking out of the ground with tree roots mixed in. All the hills get icy but there are natural staircases on the hills so mind your footing and do not be afraid to slow down when the trail gets a little narrow if inexperienced.

I’ve done this trail many times and I’m always disappointed that I never see any wild animals. Today, after a brief snow fall, I witnessed 3 deer and a very large coyote. It was a bit icy in the beginning of the trail but does improve further in the trail. This trail gives you a good work out with many elevations.
Went early on the path this morning and it was really cold out. Paths are patted down with compact snow and ice.
Beautiful

Got there early today (Friday) so no other cars in the lot. Loved the first half walking along the creek. After the bridge there were many elevation changes. Trail is narrow but easy to follow. Will definitely come back in the summer and fall!

Any trail that follows the water is great by me! Very well marked. Snow covered, but not slippery, so it was perfect for a sunny, but chilly day in nature. I actually started from Snake Road and hiked to the falls and back from there.
Icy — wear ice cleats

Completed on January 22nd. 

Parts of the trail are incredibly icy right now, especially around the waterfall, but as far as Southern Ontario has to offer in January this trail was nice. It was quite busy, as it was the weekend, but most trails in Hamilton are right now.

Beautiful trail with a ton of variety. Everything from a Waterfall, Creekside trail, Marsh, dense forest, pond and escarpment views.

Moderate trail with decent elevation sections.
Great workout

Did the Upper Grindstone Side trail this morning. A lovely little offshoot of the Smokey Hollow Trail.  Isn't too long and just enough hills to get the heart pumping. I heard some woodpeckers in the forest and saw a deer out in the fields. The scenery is always changing each day I visit here. A tried and true favorite path of mine.
Great trail can be difficult but nonetheless amazing would definitely recommend.
muddy
Great trail. Unfortunately quite muddy and icy. But still a good hike.

Started at the waterfall, it’s about 700-800 meters of just ice! to start off. So bring your microspikes please. The trail then becomes super muddy, frozen mud and then just slippery mud. Best to bring a pair of gaiters or mud boots along. Heavily trafficked. Few moderate scrambles, overall a fun hike! Go do it.
Beautiful hilly trail. Icers needed as it’s a bit slippery.
Excellent winter wonderland hike with Stavro and Alistair! A gorgeous white Christmas Boxing Day hike.
We went to this trail during the non peak season (dec) so parking was not an issue. Overall, beautiful trail with moderate challenges. Bring hiking shoes as the ground can get muddy!
Lots of up and downs, very muddy, beautiful views, loved the hike! It was a good workout, definitely wear good hiking shoes.
Nice trail. Had lots of ups and downs. Pretty muddy
Busy at start but after a km most people turn around. Very slippery in the winter. Small parking lot, can park in nearby streets and walk down the hill.
Hilly, Muddy, great Grindstone Creek
Wear trekking shoes - it may be slippery. And a mask! Cause it’s crowded! Best to go at an off-peak time for parking’s very limited, too. But it sure was a great hike with the kids.
I went 6.5 from the start and turned back. The river was so beautiful. lot's of hills. loved it.

Parking lot was full - so we ended up parking on Snake Road! Won’t even bother checking the parking lot next time (it’s tight - even on a good day!) and will just park on Snake Rd; you enter virtually right midway through the trail. Great trail, with a few fun climbs!
SO busy. Don’t go on a sunny day, it’s pandemonium and narrow.
Great trail!

Thank you folks for your comments, which leading me to the trail yesterday. (It's getting popular so the parking lot on Mill St. S was crowed in the afternoon.) A nice trail! I wish I had been there earlier before the leaves fall. Next time. :-)
Awesome!
The most beautiful trail in the fall!
Great walk, most of it was within a valley so limited wind. Ideal for a fall hike to enjoy the fall colours.
Stunning trail, gets pretty busy with narrow paths.
brilliant.
Great trails, beautiful falls. Very busy and narrow so make sure you are safe. Extremely slippery when muddy. No bathrooms or picnic tables for lunch break.

Great hike! Beautiful waterfall at the start and lots of ups & downs throughout. We went while raining which I don’t recommend as the trail was very muddy making some of the downhills a bit sketchy! On a clear day I imagine it’s a great hike!
Great trail , lots of elevation, good cardio workout
Very nice. But a little muddy after rainy days. Feel a little uncomfortable when saw two snakes, but they are very small. Still strongly recommend!!

Go early in the morning. Definitely before ten am. Things get quite crazy on the weekends if you go after... also that parking lot is tiny so when you park on the surrounding streets the ticket is 35... not too bad but quite annoying. The tickets happen on streets that do not have 'no parking' signs so park in the lot if you can ;)
Incredible views in the first 2kms.  Changes in elevation provide a good workout.  Great trail!

This was a fund-raising walk for McMaster Children's Hospital Foundation. We only lost the trail a few times! :) We started at the Walmart parking lot end, and did not make it all the way to the waterfall near the other end.
I Love it!!
It was great fun. best view in within first 2 kms.

We started at Rockcliffe and took the green trail across the tracks to the Bruce trail. Took us about 2 hours to do the full trail to Smokey Hollow and then walk back via Waterdown road and #5 highway.  Leaves were amazing and creek was babbling along well. Wonderful day. We are in our late 50s and had no issues hiking this trail.

Recommend wear proper shoes for this trail as some parts are narrow and un-fenced, Fall leaves together with some muddy areas can make the trail rather slippery. Scenic with a beautiful fall and stream which can be quite serene. No washroom along the trail and parking is very limited (approximately less than 20 parking spots)
medium hard, lots of ups and down
Amazing trail!! Slightly crowded in the beginning but later you can just enjoy the hike on your own... lovely fall colours
Trail was great! Bit crowded at the start but became quiet a few kms in.

Great well marked trail with some decent elevation points . 

Good for dogs on leash
followed the water and stopped for some tea and bite to eat along the bank
Beautiful, lots of up and downs, a good intro to moderate hiking.

Went on the trail in early October. I would definitely suggest the trail. It's a very beautiful walk for all of the trail with lots to see. If you plan to follow the whole route make sure you're prepared for a good amount of up and down of hills. The trail is well marked via the Blaze System so you shouldn't have problems following the trail. 

If you just want to see the waterfall it is right at the beginning of the trail.

Little slippery near the water on rocks. Crowded near the falls but good for the rest. Good challenge of ups, downs, and rocky footing. Could have explored further, but was worried about it getting dark. Quite secluded and only a small section was near private property. Portion near the waterfall is very very magical and quite close to the cute town of Waterdown. I’d recommend starting at the other end (maybe near the tunnel which crosses hwy 6 - there are a few parking spots on the west side of the highway), waking into Waterdown for lunch/tea/books/exploring and then walking back.
Parking was free, the trail was okay, very muddy today especially due to the rain.

The trail was beautiful. There is a waterfall right at the entry. It would have been 5 stars if it wasn’t so busy. 

If the parking lot is full, there is a municipal parking at Dundas and Mill.
Needed to come see the fall colours come alive, so we’ll be back soon!
Awesome hike - lots of diversity in terrain. Great workout with a few good uphills!

Just beginning to change colour for fall, should be beautiful within a few more days. Has a designated parking lot, and an easy to follow trail, you can turn back at any point. Lots of inclines and elevation as well. Beautiful waterfall at the beginning of the trailhead.
Absolutely beautiful trail this time of year. Forest, creeks, trees some rocky escarpment. First time doing the trail and I loved it. I did 7 km and my legs are tired!

Nice trail with good up/down workout. We were in the shade majority of the time. So perfect for the last warm day of the autumn. The only thing is parking lot is very small. We were there at 10am but the lot was full already so we parked at Mountain brow road. There is NO sign saying no parking. But we were all got the tickets which is just not fair. So be warned.

Great dirt trail with lots of rocks and roots to watch out for.  Lots of steps/elevation changes (especially near waterfall) which could be difficult for small dogs/children. Trail follows river for good amount of time with paths down if you want to climb rocks/travel down the riverbed.  Very Busy Trail! Not for those looking for a peaceful walk!  Overall - Wonderful Trail, would do again!
Great hike, down elevation and dirt paths, more of an uneven ground. Super fun!

Beautiful trail with lots of hills and gorgeous view! Took the entire 10km to tire out my husky lol. 
Wish the stream/river had more flowing water like I remember it having years ago.

Really nice trail! Marked well. Waterfall was beautiful. You can walk right up to it snd take pictures. On a less crowded day, you could probably even bathe in it. 

Medium-traffic.
First half is beautiful but it gets a little close to roads. A few hills made it a decent hike. Would definitely do again.
I really enjoyed this hike, I was hoping it wouldn’t be too easy and It turned out to be a decent challenge. Would definitely recommend wearing hiking boots, the trail can be quite rocky at times.

Just hiked the trail on Sunday!! I loved it! It was  a bit busier then I would prefer to thats to be expected on the weekend. It was well marked, lots of roots great elevations, so nice workout. Parking is very limited, not sure why they don’t make that area bigger. We were lucky to have gotten a spot. Leave early

You start at the highlight which is kinda awesome and kinda sucks lol. But there are a lot of elevation changes and rocky portions, especially toward the end of the trail as listed here for the more experienced hiker. I did not double back on the trail, and instead did a sort of loop through a side trail and Waterdown itself. If I doubled back it would've been longer than the 10km listed here.
Great spot!
Excellent trail - great stretch of the BT. Highly recommended for a great hike with lots of elevation and beautiful forest.
A ton of hills and stairs. Great for cardio

Great trail. Started at the Waterdown parking lot.  Trail has just enough inclines to make it an interesting hike. No bugs and clearly marked trails. Thanks to the member clubs who maintain this section of the Bruce trail.

Didn’t have time to walk the entire trail, but will definitely need to come back. The trail along Grindstone Creek is quite irregular with plenty of exposed roots and rocks so watch your step. Great opportunities for photographers.

Amazing hike. We also parked in the Walmart parking lot and began at the storm water system. Beginning was abit rocky, but nothing that any child wouldn't be able to handle. There were many elevation changes which made this 10.5k hike feel like a small workout. Balzes were well marked as this is a part of the Bruce with may options to take side trails. Trail was busy near the falls, but nealy nearly vacant for about 7k.

great hike along a small river before venturing off of it. parking was not easy as the lot is very small and need to go into town to park. a lot of people at the very start of the trail because of a small waterfall. hike for about 10 minutes and it'll become less busy. I would do it again.
The trail was great nice variety! Intermediate hike! Lots of people near Smokey Hallow!
Such a beautiful trail! And it can get quite rough too. Definitely one of the top hiking trails in my opinion.
Well marked trail with decent amount of elevations. Would suggest arriving early as the parking lot is pretty small and gets filled up real quick.

A lovely hike. Lots of roots and rocks at the beginning (the falls) and more heavily trafficked. There are fewer people further along the trail, which follows the creek and winds up and down hills in the forest. Watch out for mountain bikers.
Super nice scenery, and pretty kids friendly. There was a nice waterfall, which made the trail quite cool for a summer day.

Well marked, lots of elevations, excellent leg workout, lots of green landscapes, overall very nice trail. We parked at the Walmart parking lot and started at the tail of the trail. It worked pretty well as we hiked through the woods, took a break at the Falls and then hiked back.

It’s really not worth the hassle of small parking lot, difficulty parking on nearby streets is crowded and the locals call police so tickets handed out for infractions There are other places that are better People crowding in falls and Id stay clear
Go early. The parking is awful. Last time a car side swiped my car. Didn’t notice till later. So bummed. Today we went at 8:15 . Great time to go. When we were done it was just getting busy

We did the whole trail in 2.5h which was quite a bit of leg work for little gain (there was no view). Make sure you follow they trail markers, it’s really easy to get lost because the trail intersects with others, like a mountain bike trail. You will need hiking boots. The “view” (Smokey hollow waterfall) was at the trailhead but there were too many people making a ruckus just for the gram. Parking lot had a constant overflow of cars and many ended up in “no parking” spots - turnover is constant though so you just have to wait for the right timing.
Really great trail! Well kept, beautiful scenery and a great workout. Be careful at the falls - the rocks can get slippery

Went with a group of friends and took us about 4.5hrs because of some detours and chilling at the Falls. Trail is well marked, moderate - hard, with lots of changes in terrain. Definitely recommend good grip hiking shoes and taking a change of clothes because the waterfall is enticing to jump in! It's only waist drop and quite rocky. If you get lost, back track to find the white trail marks for Bruce Trail. We parked at the Walmart parking lot and started at the tail end of the trail so there was ample parking. I would recommend starting there as you hike through the woods, enjoy and rest at the Falls then hike back, instead of the other way around! Bonus was we went on a Friday and it wasn't heavily trafficked at all! Observation deck is now open.

Absolutely amazing. I ran and hiked it. What a amazing find. Can’t wait to come back. It’s a little difficult so good footwear is a must. And definitely come early because it gets busy. I arrived at 9:15 but probably should of came for 8
Best trail ever’

Parked at smoky hollow and walked all the way to the little cute pond at the end of the trail, got a bit lost when on the way back as not pay attention to the White trail sign...lol~ a good day hike, did in 5 hours... Love it~
Nice! Overall we enjoyed the hike. Limited space for parking.
Crowded
Challenging and awesome

Loved this hike! We arrived around 9:20 and parking was full, but people were leaving regularly. There are MANY elevation changes and rocky/rooted paths - which made it challenging and fun. We had 2 dogs and they had a great time too. Lots of photographic areas - rivers, bridges, great trees, moss covered logs.
I loved this trail, lots of varying terrain, beautiful waterfall!
Great hike - best done early in the morning if you're like me and like to be alone in nature. Parking lot is very small and narrow, and fills up later in the morning.
Great trail!  Enjoyed the elevation changes, had to watch my step with the many roots, and it is not a loop, had to turn back as it continues for quite some time! A+

great trail with beautiful views. Very long trail with lots of inclines. *warning* Do not park at the actual parking on-site space is very limited and tight and your car will probably get hit! People don't care I saw someone's car get hit and mine did as well and no one left info.
Excellent trail for workout - felt like real hiking, loved the experience, this is not a loop though, you need to turn back when low on energy!
Good workout for the legs little hard on the knees

Great hike with lots to see and explore! Waterfall at the beginning where you park.   Parking is very limited even at 9am.  Walked to the end and took a back route to the Walmart for a beak before waking back.   Followed some bike trails which where easier till we got back to snake road.
It’s a great trail and a good leg workout if you do it at a decent pace. Better to go when it’s not busy to avoid traffic on the stairs. There is very limited parking.

A great leg workout, lots of ups and downs throughout the trail. Quite rooty in places so watch your step! Would recommend going early as the parking lot gets quite busy on the weekend. Inukshuks were really neat to look at.

Great trail! Got there early to get parking and avoid the crowds which builds up steadily during the day. To get to the base of the waterfall you have to navigate boulders, so wear good shoes. I would rate this trail as moderate.
Great hiking trail. Go early to get parking. Full shade and a great leg workout. Distance is 6.5km one way. Plan for 3-3.5 hours for return.
Moderate, but not for rookies like me. Legs, hills rocks and roots. Really good trail!!!
so nice! decent leg workout. nice refreshment in the water afterwards. come as early as 9 am to get a place on the parking lot at the waterfall

This is a majestic trail, inclines and declines and twists and turns...beauty trees and fungus and moss! I love moss!! Smokey Hollow Falls was very crowded and...i didn’t really like that. There was a lot of waiting to go around people on the trail. However, my friend, dog and I decided to kick our shoes off and climb off the trail, down the hill and into the big massive boulders/rocks in the water. It was a nice way to avoid humans, and have a little adventure in the water. We also had a picnic on the rocks. Ton of fun!!! If you want to avoid crowds, I’d choose to go on a weekday or slightly rainy day when the majority of people might skip it. Also, be mindful where you park. I got a parking ticket.

Lots of forks on the trail, but most of them lead back to the main trail. Overall the trail is nice, elevation gain is happening throughout so be prepared for a leg workout! Parking lot was open by the falls.
Great trail. Parking by the falls was opened.

BEWARE - Parking near the trail entrance is closed. Authorities have barricaded the parking entrance but someone removed the barricades in the morning and many drivers parked the cars thinking parking was opened. While we came back we saw all parked cars had gotten the tickets ($55). Don't park in the lot unless it specifically mentioned on their website. Nearest parking (2 hours limit) is on Main St near Union St. Trail entrance is 5 mins walk from here. 

Wear appropriate shoes if planning to go near the falls.

10/10 trail! Lots of elevation, main trail is well maintained, can get rocky in some parts. There’s also a stream that follows you along for a bit of the trail that gives off a nice cooling effect. Pups are welcomed, single file for most of the trail so good for social distancing. As mentioned on other reviews, the main parking lot is closed but there’s lots of residential streets to park on (closest one is about a 5 minute walk from the trail) or you can park at a park close by. Can’t wait to visit again!
Good one but if you plan to do entire 10km, get good shoes and water. Fairly demanding
Great for hiking

Amazing trail. We went all the way down to snake road. Overall it was around 5 km down and back. It's kid friendly if they are in for the adventure. If you are looking for parking, park in the Sealey park and walk from there.
Amazing trail!!I will definitely go back!
Parking lot is closed, we parked at sealey park then walked over. The trail is beautiful and nicely shaded.

parking lot is closed but you can park on the next available residential street. beautiful trail, lots of chipmuks! I personally love challenges but there are A LOT of hills and stairs. if you enjoy a challenge take the hike!
Amazing I will come back.

The parking was open and the trail was open. FYI. Lovely trail with a beautiful Creek. Your heart rate will go up with some of the hills but nothing a healthy adult or kid can't handle. I've done this trail a bunch of times, would definitely do it again. It's somewhere between moderate and easy depending on the part of the trail you're at.
it was nice at the beginning but its incredibly boring

Parking lot was closed. We parked on Union Street and everyone else did as well so it didn't seem to be an issue. Can be challenging at the beginning because of the mud. Wear good shoes. Lot's of varied landscapes which makes for an interesting walk. Some hills towards Waterdown Road and Snake Road.
best in gta
Beautiful waterdown, highly recommended to most hiking levels.

Beautiful little spot. Parking is a bit of a challenge as there is only a very small lot. Can overlook the falls right at the beginning of the path. If you keep walking a little it’ll bring you to the bottom and you can fairly easily get yourself closer to the waterfall. The path doesn’t loop unless you want to spend half the hike on residential streets. But it’s so beautiful that having to just turn around and walk it again isn’t bad. My friends and I were able to turn this short hike into a few hours because we took the time to enjoy the beauty of everything. Highly recommend this trail :)
Will visit again, it’s one of the best trail. Worth carrying Camera.

Nice trail with some decent elevation gain as well. Is crowded. 
Couple of small side trail options as well. Saw a small snake near snake road.
Parking lots are closed in May 2020, had to find a spot on street.

Just finished 4 hours hiking with my kids (10,6,3). A bit tough for our 3yr to walk down and up the hill, but nothing to change the fact that this trail is ver recommended. Not very busy with tons of shade. Parking was the only challenge, so ended up parking just before the railroad on one of the streets. 5 stars.

Beautiful trail not too far from Toronto. Got there in the afternoon and we were lucky enough to find a parking spot; otherwise, get there early for parking. Too crowded, so we might go back on a weekday next time.

Really enjoyable first hike of the season. Started early, parking was open with plenty of space to park. Trail was empty in the morning, ran into two groups in the first half heading out.

One thing to note is All Trails says its just over 10km but it was actually 12km to go all the way out and back.
Parking lot was open but full. Trail was a bit busy at the start but less busy the further away we got. Beautiful scenery, one of the best hikes we have done in this area!! Our kids and dog loved it!
Gorgeous trail with lovely views, river and waterfall. Can currently access on the Bruce trail at the other end on Grindstone way (that’s where I did anyway). Parking lot currently closed.
Great hike!
Great challenging hike if you do the whole thing. Took me about 3 hours out and back, but the first half is pretty dog and kid friendly.

awesome

Lovely trail...but because of thick and slippery ice, much of the trail itself (and especially the stairs down into the valley) was dangerous. Be prepared with solid hiking footwear. Or wait for a good thaw.
One of my favourite trails-beautiful in all seasons.

Really pretty trail, definitely echoing other reviews that this is for sure a hike, not a walk. Can't imagine how lovely it must be in the summer if it's this nice in December. Bruce trail is always well marked, if you're planning on coming around this season expect LOTS of mud.

Great trail, good workout with different terrains and lots of different elevations. Recommend hiking boots.
beautiful fall trail. a lot of highway noise at part of the trail
Great trail less than an hour from Toronto. Trail was an in and out, nice waterfall feature, well marked and the right amount of strenuous. Highly recommend for a nice day trail!

This trail was exactly what I was looking for.
Starting from Waterdown Rd. entrance the parking is very small but we go a spot (it was Thanksgiving Weekend). The start was very...steps and roots/rocks, probably a high “moderate” but once you persevered thru the tough spot for 10 minutes you got down to a flat also beautiful hike. 
All right beside a waterfall/river/stream.

Dogs love it. Great for whole family. But it is a “hike” rather than a walk in the forest lol
really fun trail for a good workout.  you get full cellular service for the whole trail.

went there last month when it was pretty dry. beautiful trail, lots of up and down, roots and other obstacles. wear good hiking shoes, especially after rains. plan to go tomorrow afternoon. parking may or may not be available.

Great hike... More elevation changes than we were expecting so a very good workout. No bugs at all at the end of September but still very nice out. This trail is beautiful, especially at this time of year. I did not complete all of it but will definitely be back to do the while 10K. Lots of roots/rocks/steps so is a good workout! Took my dog and she loved it!
The trail is kind of boring and the waterfall is hit or miss meaning sometimes it’s there and sometimes it’s dried up.
Really nice trail

Viewing point at the top of the trail for the waterfall is open again. Website advises this trail closes mid October. Brought a lunch and sat on the rocks by the creek to listen to the water rest. Did not do the whole thing. At the 5km mark be careful of the bridge it is damaged and rocks side to side, careful footing will get you across safely. Beautiful scenery, I will do this again
loved this trail. very advantageous and eye opener. would do again.

very nice trail along the creek and starts with the waterfall, I enjoyed it very much, it is not for bikes, You can enjoy the water flow sound most of the time...we managed to sit on the rocks in the middle and enjoy the air and water sound.
the parking very small, Do not park at the road side, you will get a ticket.

The viewing point for the waterfall is closed but you can hike down to get a closer look. Great side trails, I went during the week and there were not many people on the trail. Trail is clearly marked.
A pretty tough trail.   Lots of hills/steps.   Pretty views.  Gorgeous bridge about 4km in.  I don’t think I’d rate it as moderate though.   Will definitely do it again when I want a good workout.
Really enjoyed this trail. Lots of inclines, so be prepared. Busiest section is at the beginning closer to the waterfall, but it thins out as you get farther in. Very dog friendly as well.

Starts with a waterfall and then follow the creek as you start your hike.  Some nice points to rest if needed.  Loved the terrain. A bit muddy in spots from the recent rain.  Not too many bugs until deeper in the forest.
Great trail. Some downed trees across main trail. Follow the new trail around them back to the main trail and your good to go.
Beautiful trail! Not for strollers and young babes. But the water alongside was so beautiful. Be prepared for inclines  and lots of tree roots, loved it!
Nice place for an easy hike or trail run. Not stroller friendly, but good for dogs.
This trail is so beautiful and calming. I loved being alongside the river. Our dog loved it too! He was able to cool of at a few points!

Nice rolling elevation and some changes of scenery, including crossing an active railway track! Extremely buggy but likely due to the many wet days preceding.

Lovely trail! Waterfall is at the beginning, nice elevation, brooks and streams running through it. Very quiet/remote, just one road and train track to cross. Went with Bernie and Faiz, carried 30lbs for mountaineering training, but forgot hiking boots!

great trail! Took my two dogs out with my boyfriend. Might need to mention though to wear sheady shoes. Very steep at points and not meant for older dogs.
Make sure you bring sturdy, waterproof shoes! Very muddy in some parts, but very worth it.

The best part about this trail that you're accompanied by the sound of Creek, the trail is just along the water and gives enough chances to go up and down. you can speed up and slow down as you like, a lot of pets were enjoying the hike too! unfortunately, it was too muddy at some points so it is ideal to visit this spot during peak summers. Also, very few parking spots, morning hours are the best to find one!
Should not be rated easy.
Amazing, very challenging trail. My legs were burning the whole time with all the ups and downs. After the first couple km’s you get lots of moments of solitude
I loved it
Smokey Hollow Falls is gorgeous, terrific gorge hike with water features and interest throughout.
There were so many off-leash dogs in the parking lot we left.

it's a beautiful trail, very well marked I never got lost in this trail although this app says it's 10.3k out and back which it is not. I ended up doing almost 18k out and back so be prepared for that! I would say this is moderate in winter time with the snow and ice but it is an easy trail overall.

everything I want in a trail - water fall, large rocks, the creek to follow, tall trees , some inclines, a path with a little bit of a challenge to it and free parking. only did a few km's in it was beautiful. will plan to do the entirety when I have time. note it should be listed as moderate rather than easy

Lots of amazing views such as the upper quarry cascade  at the waterdown start point, the snake falls, boundary falls, grindstone cascade and the most beautiful of all, the great falls or smokey hollow falls. The trail itself is gorgeous with all the wood additions to help guide and support hikers. A must trail to travel especially in the winter although its slippery and muddy, but definately worth it!

Great area for exercise but I would say it’s moderate not easy. Just because there are so many steps and some double sized ones. 
Tight edges in some places a little stressful when slippery due to weather and need to give way for in coming traffic to pass. I would recommend hiking shoes in this trail. 
Some may find it challenging on the way down but consider this trail loops and double the work going up on the return. 
Over all it’s a great area.
Great trail not well market. Could get lost without guide.
Just awesome.  Vibrant fall colours and great hiking experience for all ages.

Moderate trail. Great for bigger dogs, my lab had the best time, lots of water for him to splash in. Decent amount of people in the beginning but thinned out as you got further in. Parking is very limited but free. No garbage cans throughout the trail, just an FYI. Lots of diversity of scenery, enjoyable hike.
one of my fave's
My highly active 5yr old managed ok but its definitely a moderate trail.
Definitely moderate and hard for a dog to walk
Moderate for the beginners.
Awesome hike with Meetup group.  I missed recording the first hour or so...lots of elevation changes.  good water flow on falls...can't seem to delete the duplicate photos...

I would not rate this trail as easy. Moderate at best. The roots and rocks make for a very bumpy terrain and the multiple sets of stairs on the way back will work every part of your body. It is a gorgeous trail and worth doing just be prepared for cardio day!!

We went with our 3 year olds.  It was moderate hike for them if you stay on the trail.  It was a long one for their tiny legs, but found a few nice spots for snack breaks. It is definitely a beautiful hike, I'd definitely recommend.

Beautiful trail but I would not rate this as easy or kid friendly. If you have older kids (7 years and up) maybe. It gets steep at times and the wooden steps are slippery after rains and metal poles stick out of the ground at unexpected places along the trail. Needs to be better maintained. The creek and waterfall are beautiful, however you often hear road sounds so it’s not a complete serene hike. Many dog walkers leave behind bags of dog waste which ruins it for everyone else. There is a trash bin at the start of the trail near the waterfall and parking is small (and they issue tickets when parked outside the lot boundary). The trail connects with another section of Bruce Trail so you can park somewhere else and hike a bit longer to avoid the parking mayhem.
It’s all nature and peace. Wonderful waterfall and a  beautiful trail. Lots of rocks and roots cause ups and down in the trail.

Beautiful!  I would say this is more of a moderately difficult trail as opposed to the advertised easy due to up and down stairs and walking through rooted paths. Easy to me would mean flat wide trails. Can’t wait to go back in the fall!
An absolutely beautiful trail that starts at the waterfall. Easy to maneuver around the rocks, fallen trees and Staggered terrain. Perfect for the nature enthusiast like myself.
Walking along with the creek. Wanderful waterfall! Very nice place for Hiking.

Great trail for getting little ones interested in hiking. Lots of roots and rocks to negotiate around. Waterfall views and river sound is awesome. Trees have fallen and block the path in a few spots. Girls had a blast and both fell asleep in the truck on the way home. Truly impressed to all those who put the time in to make the trail what is. Thank you.
Entrance from mill st is very steep, many stairs. After you get past the descend it's great! Try it out.
Can't beat a trail where all you hear is nature and rushing water
Great for a winter hike!

Great trail along the river bank. Bruce Trail started off with a waterfall, then straight down hill. Lots of up and down hills and great views. Small parking lot at Mill Street South and Waterdown Rd. No fee.

Good size waterfall! Apparently spring is the prime time to go for water flow, however fall allowed us to walk through it as it was gentle enough. Decent access to the falls, still accessible to explore, not fenced off like some. Good set of trails attached to this waterfall. (Sometimes there’s not much to do other than be directly at the falls). Interesting section of the Bruce for a city stretch, nice that it has loop options.
Muddy terrain with lots of hills. Amazing views of the waterfall and the trail follows the river for a little while! I really liked the challenge and the calming feeling of the area.
I thought the trail was great.
Really nice hike,  beautiful waterfall and path along the river.

A tough start (steep stairs and inclines) gives way to a moderate hike. Worth the effort due to the beautiful scenery. Parking near the entrance on Mill St is limited so I suggest using parking at the Dundas St intersection then walking up.

For a 12km  there-and-back, the reward for the “there” is the back of a Walmart. It takes you out of the hike when all of a sudden you’re back in civilization. We did stop and get a snack at Walmart since we could. A funny aside, but the trail was moderately challenging with many hills. Many parts were muddy today, but it was not a big detractor.
